'''Tin''' is a crafting material smelted from [[Tin Ore]] in a [[Smelter]].

Just like [[Copper Ore]], [[Tin Ore]] can only be found in the [[Black Forest]] [[Biomes|biome]]. It takes the form of small shiny rock-like deposits on the ground near water (ocean & river shorelines, or small inland lakes).

An [[Antler Pickaxe]] or better is required to mine the rocks, which yield 2-4 Tin ore each.

One Tin can be processed with two [[Copper]] on the [[Forge]] to create one [[Bronze]]. There is also an alternate recipe to craft 5 Bronze at a time given sufficient materials (10 copper, 5 tin).

'''Yellow Mushrooms''' are commonly found in [[Burial Chambers]] or [[Troll Cave]]s in the [[Black Forest]], and [[Sunken Crypts]] in the [[Swamp]].

They can be eaten raw, or used in a [[Mead Ketill]] for crafting.

As with most plants, these regrow naturally after being picked up. Picked mushrooms will respawn after 240 minutes, {{duration|14400}}. They are the ''only'' part of an underground chamber that regenerates.

[[Boar]]s will not eat Yellow Mushrooms.

'''Serpent Meat''' is a guaranteed drop from [[Serpent]]s, and drops in quantities of 6-7. It can be cooked on an [[Iron Cooking Station]] to obtain '''Cooked Serpent Meat''' and be eaten or crafted into other foods. == Availability == {{drop table|title=Creature| {{drop row|item=Serpent|0star=6-7|px=70}} |stars=0}} == Usage == === Crafting === ==== For Serpent Meat ==== * {{Item link|Cooked Serpent Meat|nolink=1}} * {{Item link|Coal}}, if left on an Iron cooking station for too long ==== For Cooked Serpent Meat ==== * {{Item link|Serpent Stew}} * {{Item link|Sailor's Bounty}} Unlike most other foods made from meat, Serpent Meat has to be cooked on an Iron cooking station first to be crafted into other foods. == Notes == * Serpent Meat floats. It can remain floating for a considerable period. If the player kills a Serpent during a storm but cannot pick up the meat at the time, return as soon as possible and the meat may still be recoverable. * As [[Serpent Stew]] provides more health and stamina, eating the meat is not ideal unless in excess of it. * The stew's constituent ingredients are easily obtainable, with [[Mushroom]]s able to be foraged from [[Meadows]] and [[Black Forest]]s, while the [[Honey]] can be obtained from [[Beehive]]s. * A player eating Cooked Serpent Meat may want to limit the amount of it they carry, as each one is much heavier than any other foods. {{FoodsNav}} [[ru:Мясо змея]] [[cs:Maso z hada]]

It is used directly in food recipes at the [[Food Preparation Table]]. == Availability == {{drop table|title=Creature| {{drop row|item=Seeker|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4|px=50}} {{drop row|item=Seeker soldier|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4|px=50}} }} == Usage == === Crafting === ==== For Seeker meat ==== * {{Item link|Cooked seeker meat|nolink=1}} * {{Item link|Coal}}, if left on an Iron cooking station for too long * {{Item link|Meat Platter}} (from {{Item link|Uncooked Meat Platter}}) * {{Item link|Seeker Aspic}} ==== For Cooked seeker meat ==== * {{Item link|Mushrooms Galore á la Mistlands}} Cooked seeker meat cannot be used to craft recipes using Seeker meat as ingredient, or vice versa. == Notes == * For magic-oriented players, the [[Seeker Aspic]] is the best Eitr-granting food available in the Mistlands. * Because there are many [[Seeker]]s in the Mistlands and the production of [[Meat Platter]]s tends to be bottlenecked behind the rarer [[Hare Meat]], Cooked seeker meat can serve as a good food option when the player is returning to older biomes or working on base building. {{FoodsNav}} [[ru:Мясо искателя]] [[cs:Maso Hledačů]]
